headline: Bitcoin ETFs shed $636M in a day as institutional appetite cools across the board
summary: A sharp reversal in Bitcoin ETF flows — $636 million in net outflows erasing the prior session's gains — pulled Bitcoin down 1.27% to $80,617 and dragged most of the top 20 lower. The selloff was broad rather than deep, with altcoins like Solana, XRP, and Dogecoin each falling 2–4%. Against that backdrop, Franklin Templeton quietly tokenized $150 million in fund shares on the XRP Ledger, a reminder that institutional infrastructure work continues even on down days.

winners.name: MemeCore
winners.catalyst: MemeCore surged roughly 21% with no identifiable news catalyst — the move appears to be speculative retail momentum running against the broader risk-off session.

losers.name: NEAR Protocol
losers.catalyst: NEAR fell nearly 8%, underperforming the broader altcoin selloff. The $636M in Bitcoin ETF outflows dampened risk appetite across layer-1 tokens; no NEAR-specific catalyst was identified.

whyItMoved: The day's story was ETF flows, not price. Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $636 million in net outflows — reversing the prior session's inflows in a single day and marking one of the sharper single-day redemption events in recent months. When institutional money exits BTC funds at that pace, it tends to pull the broader market lower, and that's what happened: Bitcoin fell 1.27% to $80,617, Ethereum dropped 1.23%, and most of the top 20 followed. The selling was orderly rather than panicked — the Fear & Greed index sits at 51, squarely neutral — but the breadth was notable. Privacy coins took a harder hit: Zcash fell 4.75% and Monero dropped 3.76%, though no specific news drove those moves. XRP slid 2.79% despite a genuinely positive institutional development — Franklin Templeton tokenized $150 million in fund shares directly on the XRP Ledger, all held in a single wallet. That kind of real-money institutional adoption would normally be a tailwind, but it wasn't enough to offset the day's broader risk-off tone driven by the ETF outflow data. NEAR Protocol was the session's worst performer among major assets, falling 7.91% — a steeper drop than peers, though no NEAR-specific catalyst emerged. The most likely explanation is that layer-1 tokens with smaller liquidity bases tend to absorb more selling pressure when institutional flows reverse.
worthKnowing: Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand's central banks expanded a cross-border stablecoin payment corridor that now includes Ripple, Visa, and Mastercard — a sign that regulated stablecoin infrastructure is advancing in Southeast Asia.
Bitcoin Core updated its vulnerability disclosure policy to account for AI tools that can now identify protocol bugs far faster than human researchers alone.

Senator Blumenthal sent a formal inquiry to Tether demanding details on payments made to a firm founded by a former White House crypto adviser, adding a new thread of regulatory scrutiny to the stablecoin issuer.
